blocks.text: Network diagnostic tools are used to find network problems. They help check internet and network connections. These tools show whether devices can communicate properly. Commands are entered using the command prompt or terminal. It helps identify slow or broken connections.

Network troubleshooting is done to find and fix network issues. It helps detect connection and speed problems. Troubleshooting checks cables, devices, and settings. It reduces network downtime and errors. It helps maintain smooth communication. Proper troubleshooting improves network performance.

The ping command is used to test network connectivity. It checks if a device is reachable on the network. Ping sends small data packets to another device (as shown in Figure 1.16). It measures response time from the destination. This command helps detect network delays. It is commonly used to check internet connection.

Ipconfig is used in Windows operating system. Ifconfig is used in Linux and macOS systems. These commands display network settings. They show IP address and subnet mask. They also show gateway and network status. These commands help in network troubleshooting.

Telnet is used for remote device access. It sends data without encryption. PuTTY is a popular tool for remote login. SSH is a secure method for remote access. SSH encrypts data for safety. These tools help manage network devices.
